To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the use of a poly (acrylic acid)-modified microchip allows for the separation of a mixture of catecholamine neurotransmitters, which is not possible in an unmodified microchannel.

the modification of the surface of glass electrophoretic microchips with poly (acrylic acid), a polymer that has not been used before in microchip electrophoretic applications, allows the partial resolution of a mixture of three catecholamines: dopamine, epinephrine and norepinefrine.

(i) a new glass microchannel modification based on PAA immobilization is proposed, (ii) it was successfully employed to the resolution enhancement of catecholamine microchip electrophoretic separation and (iii) this modification is compatible with amperometric detection.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a new surface modification of microchips for the enhanced resolution in microchip electrophoretic analysis of catecholamine neurotransmitters.
the development of a new modification for the enhancement of the separation resolution of catechols in microchips.
the development of a new microchip modification that can be easily performed and that can be applied to the separation of catecholamine mixtures.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
a 60 mm channel microchip with 3% methanol is the most suitable system, since it provides the best resolution and the shortest run time.

the modification of the glass surface with PAA, in combination with a suitable organic modifier (MeOH), is an effective way to improve the separation of catecholamine mixtures by CE with amperometric detection in glass microchips.
the modification of the microchannel surface is a very effective strategy to enhance resolution in microchip electrophoretic separation of catecholamine mixtures, even in the case of short channels.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the use of PAA as coating material is suitable to enhance the resolution of catecholic compounds in microchip electrophoretic separations, but it is not enough for a full separation of the three catecholamines.
the modification of the microchannel with PAA is an effective tool for improving the resolution of the analytes, and the use of methanol as organic modifier is also a good strategy to enhance it.

the immobilization of PAA on glass microchips is an effective method for the resolution of the catecholamines, even when a short separation length is employed, and that the addition of methanol as organic modifier is a useful tool to enhance the resolution.
The main takeaway from our work is that
PAA microchannel modification can be used to enhance the separation of a catecholamines mixture in microchips with an effective length of 60 mm, employing amperometric end detection.
the microchannel surface modification is a powerful and easy to implement tool for improving the separation efficiency of microchip electrophoretic systems.
the microchannel modification procedure is simple and fast, and it allows for the resolution enhancement of catecholamine mixtures.
